creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Passing `headers=` alongside `json=` drops the automatic `Content-Type: application/json`, so Jira answers 415. One condition at `core/funcs.go:1951-1953`: `if headersArg.IsNull()` wants to be "unless Content-Type is already set".

Documented as a wart twice in live scripts - `raiselog:120-121` ("it must be given explicitly - Jira 415s otherwise") and `snapstore-push:29` - and `work:274` pays the same tax. The review called it the clearest single fix in its report.

---

### Orientation
- Confirmed: the condition is exactly where the card says. `core/funcs.go:1951-1953` is `if headersArg.IsNull() { headers["Content-Type"] = ... }`, inside the shared `Execute` closure that all nine `http_*` builtins are built from by `createHttpFunctions()` (`core/funcs.go:1890-1966`).
- One edit fixes all nine methods.
- The user's `headers=` map is flattened into the Go `headers` map just above, at `core/funcs.go:1917-1932`.

### Where to start
- `core/funcs.go:1946-1954` - the `json=` branch. Replace the `headersArg.IsNull()` test with "unless a Content-Type is already present in `headers`".
- The lookup has to be case-insensitive. `headers` is keyed by the user's literal string (`keyStr` at `core/funcs.go:1922`), so a script writing `content-type` produces a different Go map key than `Content-Type`. Walk the keys and compare with `strings.EqualFold` rather than indexing.
- All nine `docs/funcs/http_*.md` carry the same sentence on line 32: "sets `Content-Type: application/json` when no headers are supplied". That is now wrong and must be reworded in every file, then `make generate`.

### How to verify
```sh
make build
go test ./core/testing/ -run TestSnapshots -update=functions/http
go test ./core/testing/
make generate && make verify-generated
```
Snapshot suite is `core/testing/snapshots/functions/` (`http_get.snap`, `http_post.snap`). Tests capture outgoing requests through a callback registered at `core/testing/test_helpers.go:136`, accumulating into `httpInvocations`.

### Done when
- `json=` plus an unrelated `headers=` (e.g. only `Authorization`) still sends `Content-Type: application/json`.
- An explicit `Content-Type` in `headers=` still wins, in any letter case.
- All nine doc files reworded and `make verify-generated` clean.
- Snapshot cases cover: json alone, json plus unrelated headers, json plus explicit Content-Type, json plus lowercase `content-type`.

### Watch out for
- There is no existing helper that asserts on request headers - `core/testing/test_helpers.go` only has `assertHttpInvocationUrls` (:568) and `assertHttpInsecure` (:590). Either add a header assert helper next to them or read `httpInvocations[i].RequestDef.Headers` directly.
- `core/requester.go:178-182` applies headers with `req.Header.Add`, which canonicalizes the key. If the map ends up holding both `content-type` and `Content-Type`, both get added under the same canonical name and the request goes out with a duplicated Content-Type. The case-insensitive check above is what prevents that.
- Stay behind the `RReq` seam (`core/global.go:44`) - `core/testing/` injects a Requester with mocked responses.
title: http: stop headers= suppressing the json= Content-Type
